newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to sell Gulf Insurance shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to sell Gulf Insurance shares.

text.p: Kuwait will sell a second stake in Gulf Insurance Company worth 25 million dinars ($83.4 million) by public auction, the Kuwait News Agency reported on Friday.
It quoted officials as saying the two-week public subscription for 50 million shares at 510 fils a share starts on September 29.
The share closed at 560 fils on Wednesday. Kuwait's five-day trading week starts on Saturday.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.

The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, in June sold 20 million Gulf Insurance shares for 12.6 million dinars and said it would sell another 50 million -- a total of 70 million shares or a 62 percent stake. KIA originally had a 75 percent stake in the company.
Gulf Insurance made a net profit rise of 11 percent to 2.9 million dinars in 1995. Earnings per share stood at 26.21 fils in 1995 compared to 23.60 fils the previous year.
Kuwait plans to sell state holdings is 60 local firms ahead of a more complex stage of privatising public services like water electricty and telecommunications.
